question: Should OpenClaw support generic scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*` in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, now that the official Chrome extension has a paired `/browser/extension` route?
rationale: This changes a Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary, and the current code/docs intentionally expose only exact full origins plus the global allow-all `*`; current related PRs do not settle the security semantics.

options.title: Keep exact origins plus paired route
options.body: Reject generic scheme wildcards for now and direct official Chrome-extension users to the paired `/browser/extension` route while exact-origin fixes continue separately.

options.title: Approve a constrained wildcard grammar
options.body: Allow a narrowly specified `chrome-extension://*` policy with explicit tests, docs, audit handling, and clear limits on which schemes can be wildcarded.

options.title: Fold into broader origin patterns
options.body: Wait for the `allowedOriginPatterns` design to settle and decide whether Chrome-extension scheme wildcards belong in that separate contract instead of overloading `allowedOrigins`.

recommendation.title: Keep exact origins plus paired route
recommendation.body: Reject generic scheme wildcards for now and direct official Chrome-extension users to the paired `/browser/extension` route while exact-origin fixes continue separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the strongest history across the original Gateway origin hardening and the newly merged official Chrome-extension route.
